metadata.title: Independent reading in rural China’s elementary schools_ A mixed-methods analysis

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses a clustered multi-stage school/class survey in rural China (134 schools; students in grades 3–6), but the provided text does not report the use of complex survey weights (e.g., sampling weights) or any replicate-weight scheme. The authors do report cluster-robust standard errors adjusted for clustering at the school level, which addresses within-school correlation for inference but is not the same as applying population-representative survey weights. No PVs are used because the outcomes are standardized scores from study-administered tests (reading adapted from PIRLS items; plus math and Chinese tests) rather than ILSA PV-based achievement scales. The analytic sample is defined by the survey administration design (all students took the reading test; math and Chinese were assigned to half of students within each class), implying missingness by design rather than item nonresponse.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variables are standardized scores from study-administered reading, math, and Chinese tests, and the paper does not describe any PV-based achievement scaling or PV combination procedure. Missing-data handling is not reported because the text frames the math/Chinese missingness as an intentional random assignment within classes (half take language, half take math), and it does not provide an explicit strategy for any additional missingness (e.g., absent students or incomplete questionnaires). This is therefore a reporting gap for missingness beyond the by-design test assignment.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Quantitative survey data were collected in Guizhou and Jiangxi provinces (six rural counties total). Schools were selected in two steps: (1) rural primary schools were drawn from within the six counties using exclusions for county-seat (urban) locations and schools with fewer than 100 students; (2) within each selected school, students in grades 3–6 were sampled by randomly selecting up to two classes per grade (all classes if ≤2). All students in sampled classes completed the reading test; within each class, students were randomly assigned to take either the math test or the Chinese-language test (half each), yielding smaller observation counts for math and Chinese. The paper does not report additional exclusions (e.g., missing covariates) in the provided text.

main_findings.dataset_used: Study-administered Reading test (PIRLS-adapted items), rural China (Guizhou & Jiangxi), grades 3–6 (2015 survey)
main_findings.performance_metrics: OLS correlations with county fixed effects; cluster-robust SEs at school level. In the full model (Table 3, column 4): Independent reading ≥60 min/day = 0.14 SD (p<0.01); School library becomes insignificant (0.03, not significant); Borrowing books from library = 0.00 (not significant); Caregivers buy books = −0.34 SD (p<0.01). R-squared (full model) = 0.058; Observations = 13,232.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using study-administered PIRLS-adapted reading test data from rural China (Guizhou & Jiangxi; grades 3–6), the study leveraged independent reading time, school library access, library borrowing, and caregiver book purchasing (plus student/family/school controls) to predict reading achievement, finding that spending ≥60 minutes/day on independent reading was positively associated with reading scores (0.14 SD), while caregiver-purchased books were negatively associated (−0.34 SD). This indicates that policies should prioritize enabling and encouraging genuine independent reading time and access to appropriate leisure books, rather than relying on remedial book purchasing alone, though the correlational design limits causal interpretation.

main_findings.dataset_used: Study-administered Math test, rural China (Guizhou & Jiangxi), grades 3–6 (2015 survey; math assigned to half of students per class)
main_findings.performance_metrics: OLS correlations with county fixed effects; cluster-robust SEs at school level. In the full model (Table 3, column 5): Independent reading ≥60 min/day = 0.13 SD (p<0.01); School library = 0.02 (not significant); Borrowing books from library = 0.06 (not significant); Caregivers buy books = −0.19 SD (p<0.01). R-squared (full model) = 0.061; Observations = 6,944.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using study-administered math test data from rural China (Guizhou & Jiangxi; grades 3–6 with math assigned to half of students per class), the study leveraged independent reading time, school library access, library borrowing, and caregiver book purchasing (plus student/family/school controls) to predict math achievement, finding that independent reading ≥60 minutes/day was positively associated with math scores (0.13 SD) while caregiver-purchased books were negatively associated (−0.19 SD). This indicates that strengthening independent reading opportunities may support broader academic outcomes, but that caregiver book-purchasing strategies may be ineffective or counterproductive when books are used as a remedial response to low performance rather than as engaging leisure reading.

main_findings.dataset_used: Study-administered Chinese-language test, rural China (Guizhou & Jiangxi), grades 3–6 (2015 survey; Chinese assigned to half of students per class)
main_findings.performance_metrics: OLS correlations with county fixed effects; cluster-robust SEs at school level. In the full model (Table 3, column 6): Independent reading ≥60 min/day = 0.14 SD (p<0.01); School library = 0.01 (not significant); Borrowing books from library = 0.01 (not significant); Caregivers buy books = −0.19 SD (p<0.01). R-squared (full model) = 0.076; Observations = 6,288.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using study-administered Chinese-language test data from rural China (Guizhou & Jiangxi; grades 3–6 with Chinese assigned to half of students per class), the study leveraged independent reading time, school library access, library borrowing, and caregiver book purchasing (plus student/family/school controls) to predict Chinese achievement, finding that independent reading ≥60 minutes/day was positively associated with Chinese scores (0.14 SD) while caregiver-purchased books were negatively associated (−0.19 SD). This indicates that independent reading time is linked to language achievement in rural settings, suggesting that education policy should focus on making appropriate leisure reading feasible and attractive, while also addressing why caregiver book purchases may reflect remedial needs and misaligned book suitability.

data.outcome_summary: This mixed-methods study analyzes rural China survey data from 13,232 students in 134 schools across Guizhou and Jiangxi provinces (grades 3–6). The quantitative component uses OLS regressions with county fixed effects and cluster-robust standard errors at the school level to correlate independent reading behaviors and book access with standardized reading, math, and Chinese test scores (math/Chinese were randomly assigned within classes to half the students). Across the full models, students who reported spending ≥60 minutes/day on independent reading scored higher in reading (0.14 SD), math (0.13 SD), and Chinese (0.14 SD), while students whose caregivers bought books scored lower in all three domains (reading −0.34 SD; math and Chinese −0.19 SD). The paper reports R-squared values of 0.058 (reading), 0.061 (math), and 0.076 (Chinese). Because the design is explicitly correlational, the authors caution that self-selection may explain associations, and the study does not report a missing-data handling strategy beyond the by-design test assignment.
